newsitem.title: UK: London sugar freight - Brazil dominate orders.
newsitem.headline: London sugar freight - Brazil dominate orders.

text.p: Orders for tonnage from Brazil dominated the sugar freight market at the start of the week, brokers said.
Cargill quoted for 3,000/3,300 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Haiti for prompt/June 20 and was still open with its recent Guatemala order to Venezuela.
It also quoted for 3,000 tonnes in bags from the Mississippi River to Callao for prompt/June dates.
Genoc was in the market with a number of orders, quoting for 15,500/16,000 tonnes in bulk from Salaverry to US Gulf/Atlantic for June 15/25.
It was also open for 12,500/14,000 in loose and/or preslung bags from Santos to Mediterranean with options of Black Sea, Red Sea, Indian Ocean and east Africa.
Genoc was seeking tonnage for 15,300 tonnes of bulk sugar from Barahona completing Rio Haina to US Gulf/Atlantic for June 15/30.
E D & F Man was also active with new business, entering the market with two south Brazil orders.
It was open for 12/14,000 tonnes in bags from Santos to Dubai for spot/prompt and 15/19,000 tonnes in bulk from Paranagua to Black Sea/Baltic for June 20/25.

Shipbrokers said Glencore was open for 14,000 tonnes min/max in bags from Santos or Paranagua to Pakistan plus options for prompt/10 days and also 14/25,000 tonnes in bulk from Santos to the Black Sea for June 21/30.
David Bruce issued a number of account orders, mostly for Thailand and some of its recent Brazil orders were thought to be still uncovered.
Bruce was open for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to South Korea for June 20/25 and 7,000 tonnes from Thailand to Prai for the same dates.
Other fresh bagged account orders came from D.K. Shipping, open for 25,000 tonnes from Brazil to Karachi for end June/early July with the option of shipping in two lots of 12,500 tonnes.
The same charterer quoted another account order for 14,000 tonnes from Santos to east Africa with options of Red Sea, Arabian Gulf, Karachi and Colombo for prompt/15 days notice.
It was also open for 39,000 tonnes in lots of 5/6,000 tonnes from Bombay to Karachi, floating a suggested freight rate of $11.
U & B Shipping was open for 13/18,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to Arabian Gulf for prompt/onwards, citing U.N. approval.
U & B was still open with its recent order for 14,000 tonnes from Santos to east Africa/Red Sea/Indian subcontinent.

Secretan was dominant with account orders, quoting for 14,000 tonnes in bulk from north Brazil to Baltic/Med/Black Sea for June 11/21 and a same-sized bagged from Santos or Paranagua to Pakistan plus options for prompt/10 days notice.
